title: The effects of lowering LDL cholesterol with statin therapy in people at low risk of vascular disease: meta-analysis of individual data from 27 randomised trials
authors: Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' (CTT) Collaborators, Mihaylova B, Emberson J, Blackwell L, Keech A, Simes J, et al.
followUp: median 4.8 years in trials of statin against control; 5.1 years in trials of more against less statin
population: Individual participant data from 22 trials of statin against control (134,537 participants) and 5 trials of more against less statin (39,612 participants), divided into five categories of predicted 5-year major vascular event risk
funder: British Heart Foundation research grant PG/08/063/25397 (Health Economics Research Centre, University of Oxford); UK Medical Research Council, British Heart Foundation, Cancer Research UK and, previously, the European Community Biomed Programme (CTSU); programme grant from the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council and grant from the National Heart Foundation, Australia (CTC). The funding sources had no involvement in the study design, data collection, analysis and interpretation, the writing of the report, or the decision to submit for publication.
authorConflicts: Most of the trials in this report were supported by research grants from the pharmaceutical industry. Some members of the writing committee received reimbursement of costs of scientific meetings from the pharmaceutical industry; two received honoraria from Solvay. The membership list names representatives of Bristol-Myers Squibb, Merck, Laboratoires Fournier, Bayer, Novartis Pharma, AstraZeneca and Pfizer as observers, and states that all collaborators had an opportunity to contribute to interpretation and drafting.
result: Rate ratio for major vascular events per 1.0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction 0.79 (95% CI 0.77 to 0.81), and 0.62 (99% CI 0.47 to 0.81) and 0.69 (0.60 to 0.79) in the two lowest categories of 5-year risk (below 5% and 5% to below 10%). Observed annual major vascular event rates in those allocated control ranged from 0.6% in the category below 5% to 9.5% in the category of 30% or more, and 3.6% overall in the 22 trials of statin against control. In participants with 5-year risk below 10%, the estimated absolute reduction was about 11 per 1000 over 5 years per 1.0 mmol/L (4.1% against 5.2%). In participants without previous vascular disease, rate ratios per 1.0 mmol/L were 0.85 (0.77 to 0.95) for vascular and 0.91 (0.85 to 0.97) for all-cause mortality. Cancer incidence rate ratio 1.00 (0.96 to 1.04).
